state_production_justification.assigned_when: 2026-09-16, during the v2 freeze, BEFORE any mammalian mechanism search
state_production_justification.operational_basis: SWS is generated by the animal's own preoptic/hypothalamic and cortico-thalamic machinery, arises spontaneously under homeostatic and circadian control, and identified sleep-active populations induce it on demand (Kroeger 2018 chemogenetic activation gives short-latency sleep).
state_production_justification.ambiguity: None material. Pharmacological agents can induce NREM-like states (NOPR agonists, Morairty 2023), but that is an experimental route into an endogenously produced state, not the state's normal production.
state_production_justification.note: Assignment did not dictate roles; the role profile was read off the literature.

axes.units: immobility; elevated arousal threshold; reduced locomotor activity
axes.notes: Uncontroversial and directly measured. Morairty 2023 add a useful boundary marker: even at the highest NOPR-agonist dose producing maximal NREM and SWA, animals were 'immediately arousable upon sensory stimulation, suggesting sleep rather than an anesthetic state'. Reversibility-on-stimulation is what separates this row from the anaesthesia rows behaviourally.

rate_amplitude.note: EEG SLOW WAVE AMPLITUDE INCREASES - SWA is the defining and dose-responsive measure (Morairty 2023). Note this is field-potential amplitude, not spike rate; neuronal firing alternates between up and down states rather than uniformly falling. The sub-measure as frozen conflates amplitude with rate, and here they diverge.

coordination.note: Slow-wave sleep is a state of INCREASED large-scale cortical synchrony. Opposite in sign to the anaesthesia rows in worm, where coordination collapses.

dynamical_organization.note: Low-frequency, highly organised oscillatory regime; spectral organisation is the scoring criterion for the state.

axes.units: EEG spectral power in the slow-wave band
axes.notes: NO A_neu SUB-MEASURE IS 'DECREASED' IN THIS ROW EITHER. Deep NREM, the archetype of a 'reduced activity state', scores increased on all three sub-measures as they are defined. The reduction that the naive framing has in mind is a reduction in RESPONSIVENESS and in high-frequency activity, neither of which the frozen sub-measures capture. This is a representational finding, not a claim that NREM is a high-activity state.

DELIBERATELY NOT SCORED, AND THE REASON IS A v2 GAP. Body temperature falls during SWS and is CAUSALLY driven by the same neurons that drive sleep (Kroeger 2018: chemogenetic VLPO-GAL activation increases sleep AND reduces body temperature). But body temperature is not metabolic rate, and the frozen axis set has no thermal axis. Scoring hypothermia as A_met would violate the section-20 separation the project depends on. Mouse cerebral or whole-body metabolic RATE across SWS was not located in this pass. Ketone-body metabolism affects sleep homeostasis in mice (Chikahisa 2014, PMID:24361452) but that is metabolism acting on sleep, not a measurement of metabolic rate during it.

cells.notes: No mouse study located testing cation-leak conductance as an SWS mechanism.

cells.ambiguity: SCOPE, AND IT IS TIGHT. The manipulation is pharmacological activation in animals whose sleep has already been PERTURBED by contextual fear conditioning; the reported effect is RENORMALISATION to that animal's own baseline, not a change from an unperturbed state. So this supports GIRK channels as sufficient to restore the state under a specific challenge, and does NOT establish that GIRK activity sets sleep in a naive animal. Graded accordingly and the restriction is carried in the perturbation record.

mechanisms.label: GIRK1/2 channel activation (ML297) restores sleep architecture after a learning challenge

roles.basis: Systemic pharmacological activation of a defined channel reverses a challenge-induced deficit in state amount and architecture. Sufficiency under challenge; not a naive-animal manipulation.

observed_effect.other: NREM sleep spindle power restored to pre-CFC baseline; effects confined to the first 6 h after a single-trial learning event; renormalisation to the animal's own pre-CFC baseline; associated with improved contextual fear memory consolidation

perturbations.statement: ML297, a recently developed candidate hypnotic agent targeting a new mechanism (activating GIRK1/2-subunit containing G-protein coupled inwardly rectifying potassium [GIRK] channels), alters sleep architecture in mice over the first 6 hr following a single-trial learning event. Following contextual fear conditioning (CFC), ML297 reversed post-CFC reductions in NREM sleep spindle power and REM sleep amounts and architecture, renormalizing sleep features to what was observed at baseline, prior to CFC.

chain.step: ML297 activation of GIRK1/2-containing channels
increased inwardly rectifying potassium conductance
restoration of post-CFC sleep architecture

molecules.name: GIRK1/2 (Kcnj3/Kcnj6) inwardly rectifying potassium channels
molecules.ortholog_relation: The worm volatile row's class-2 entry is slo-1 (BK), a different potassium channel family. SAME_PHYSICAL_CLASS only: both are potassium conductances promoting reduced activity, with no molecular correspondence.

mechanisms.proximal_physical_effect: increased potassium conductance hyperpolarising the networks that generate sleep oscillations

cells.discriminating_experiment: K-ATP/Kir6.2 has been linked to cortical activity and sleep-wake homeostasis in mouse but only in a preprint not scored here. A peer-reviewed K+ conductance test specific to SWS would fill the most conspicuous conductance hole in the mammalian sleep rows.
cells.notes: NOT_TESTED. Worth noting explicitly: K+ conductance is the textbook account of neuronal hyperpolarisation in sleep, and this pass located no primary mouse study establishing it causally for SWS.

cells.ambiguity: The phenotype is electrocortical (EEG spectral content), not sleep amount. Whether altered oscillations change sleep function is untested. PE-5 R2: AXIS SEPARATION. This manipulation moves A_neu (dynamical organisation: spectral power) with NO movement in A_beh or in state amount. Under the frozen three-axis rule it is a positive on one axis and a negative on the others, and it is the clearest case yet that 'affects the state' must be axis-qualified. The authors state the subunit 'does not play an important role in sleep initiation or maintenance'. PE-5 R2: A NEGATIVE THAT NAMES ITS OWN MECHANISM, which is rare and raises its value. The authors show inhibitory synaptic transmission in the reticular thalamic nucleus is INTACT despite disrupted postsynaptic gephyrin clusters, and conclude the loss is 'extensively compensated for'. So this is not evidence that alpha3-GABA-A receptors are irrelevant to NREM; it is evidence that the system is REDUNDANT at this node. Under the project's three-valued logic that distinction is the whole point: TESTED_NEGATIVE on necessity is not NOT_TESTED, and neither is it evidence of non-participation. The cell remains POSITIVE overall on the Gabrd/PV-interneuron mechanism; this null narrows which subunits carry the function. Note also the one thing that DID change - spindle-band power specifically at NREM-REM transitions - which is a state-BOUNDARY effect and is invisible to any measure that scores states separately.
cells.negative_assay_statement: Chronic EEG was recorded in Gabra3-knockout and wild-type mice (PMID:18485607). No difference was resolved during NREM sleep, at waking-NREM transitions, or in the response to 6 h sleep deprivation. The same recordings DID resolve two changes - lower 10-15 Hz power at NREM-REM transitions and slightly larger 11-13 Hz waking power - so the assay had demonstrated power. Whole-cell recording in the reticular thalamic nucleus showed inhibitory synaptic transmission intact despite disrupted gephyrin clusters, i.e. the null reflects developmental COMPENSATION rather than non-participation. SCOPE: applies to the alpha3 subunit only; the cell stays POSITIVE on the Gabrd/PV-interneuron and the beta1-subunit mechanisms.

mechanisms.label: delta-subunit GABA-A receptors on parvalbumin interneurons maintain normal sleep-state cortical oscillations

roles.basis: Conditional deletion altered NREM and REM EEG spectral content; viral reintroduction of Gabrd into PV+ interneurons RESCUED the REM phenotype - a loss/rescue pair on the state's electrocortical signature.

observed_effect.other: increased oscillatory activity in NREM; transient high-amplitude theta bursts in REM; rescued by viral Gabrd reintroduction into PV+ interneurons

perturbations.statement: PV delta-cKO mice showed altered spectral content of EEG during NREM and REM sleep that was a result of increased oscillatory activity in NREM and the emergence of transient high-amplitude bursts of theta-frequency activity during REM. Viral reintroduction of Gabrd to PV+ interneurons rescued REM EEG phenotypes.

chain.step: conditional deletion of Gabrd from PV+ interneurons
loss of tonic extrasynaptic inhibition of PV+ interneurons
altered NREM and REM cortical oscillations

molecules.name: Gabrd (GABA-A delta subunit) on PV+ interneurons
molecules.ortholog_relation: Worm class-3 sleep evidence is a TESTED_NEGATIVE (GABA not required for lethargus quiescence). Mouse gives a positive for a DIFFERENT readout - oscillation structure, not quiescence amount. SAME_PHYSICAL_CLASS on non-comparable endpoints; NOT a species contradiction.

mechanisms.proximal_physical_effect: loss of tonic extrasynaptic chloride conductance on fast-spiking interneurons, altering network oscillation structure

mechanisms.label: GABA-A receptor beta1 subunit shapes sleep oscillations without changing sleep amount

roles.basis: Germline knockout changes the spectral content of the state while leaving its amount and the overall sleep-wake architecture unchanged - a within-state organisation effect, not a state-generation effect.

observed_effect.other: increased delta power in NREM sleep; overall sleep-wake architecture UNCHANGED; highest beta1 binding in hippocampus and frontal cortex

perturbations.statement: beta1-/- mice have a distinct and abnormal sleep phenotype characterized by increased delta power in non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep and decreased theta activity in rapid eye movement (REM) sleep compared to beta1+/+ mice, without any change in the overall sleep-wake architecture... the GABAA receptor beta1-subunit does not play an important role in sleep initiation or maintenance but instead regulates the power spectrum.

chain.step: Gabrb1 deletion
altered spectral power within the state

mechanisms.proximal_physical_effect: altered inhibitory conductance in hippocampus and frontal cortex changing network oscillation frequency content

mechanisms.label: GABA-A receptor alpha3 subunit is NOT required for NREM sleep or for sleep homeostasis, and its loss is developmentally compensated

roles.basis: TESTED AND NEGATIVE on NREM spectral content, on waking-NREM transitions and on the response to 6 h sleep deprivation, with a mechanistic explanation (intact inhibitory transmission in nRT despite disrupted gephyrin clusters).

observed_effect.other: no EEG difference during NREM or at waking-NREM transitions; sleep-deprivation response identical; spindle-band (10-15 Hz) power LOWER at NREM-REM transitions; slightly larger 11-13 Hz waking power; no absence seizures; inhibitory synaptic transmission in nRT INTACT despite disrupted postsynaptic gephyrin clusters

perturbations.statement: EEG spectral analysis showed no difference between genotypes during non rapid-eye movement (NREM) sleep or at waking-NREM sleep transitions. EEG power in the spindle frequency range (10-15 Hz) was significantly lower at NREM-REM sleep transitions in mutant compared with wild-type mice. Enhancement of sleep pressure by 6 h sleep deprivation did not reveal any differences in the regulation of EEG activities between genotypes... Strikingly, despite the disruption of postsynaptic gephyrin clusters, whole-cell patch clamp recordings revealed intact inhibitory synaptic transmission in the nRT of alpha3-KO mice. These findings show that the lack of alpha3-GABA(A) receptors is extensively compensated for.

chain.step: Gabra3 deletion
developmental compensation preserving nRT inhibitory transmission
no change in NREM EEG or sleep homeostasis

mechanisms.proximal_physical_effect: no resolvable change in thalamocortical inhibitory function during NREM

cells.discriminating_experiment: Measure sleep amount and fragmentation, not only EEG spectra, in PV-Gabrd cKO mice, to determine whether the oscillation phenotype carries any change in the state itself.
cells.notes: NEW CELL FROM PE-5. Contrast with worm is endpoint-driven, not species-driven: worm class 3 in sleep is a TESTED_NEGATIVE for quiescence; mouse class 3 is a POSITIVE for oscillation structure.

cells.ambiguity: Same manipulation as S3_rem_mmus c4 but a DIFFERENT phenotype: NREM is fragmented rather than abolished, so the role is maintenance, not production. The authors explicitly separate sleep maintenance from sleep drive, which remained intact.

mechanisms.label: NMDA receptors on LPO GABA neurons stabilise NREM sleep-wake architecture

roles.basis: Deletion produced highly fragmented NREM sleep-wake patterns with normal TOTAL sleep and intact homeostatic drive - a consolidation phenotype, not a production one.

observed_effect.other: normal total sleep, high sleep-wake fragmentation; transiently rescued by zolpidem or dexmedetomidine; fragmentation persisted under sleep deprivation despite high propensity

perturbations.statement: When NMDA receptors are selectively reduced from inhibitory preoptic neurons, mice have normal total amounts of sleep but high sleep-wake fragmentation, providing a model for studying intractable insomnia.

chain.step: GluN1 deletion from LPO GABA neurons
destabilised firing of sleep-on neurons; fragmented NREM

molecules.name: Grin1 / GluN1
molecules.ortholog_relation: EXACT_MOLECULE shared with S3_rem_mmus c4, DIFFERENT ROLE (MAINTAINS vs PRODUCES).

mechanisms.proximal_physical_effect: loss of ionotropic excitatory drive onto preoptic GABAergic sleep-on neurons
mechanisms.overlap_resolution: EXACT_MOLECULE vs S3_rem_mmus c4, DIFFERENT ROLE

cells.notes: NEW CELL FROM PE-5. THE SAME MOLECULE AND THE SAME EXPERIMENT YIELD A DIFFERENT ROLE IN THE TWO SLEEP ROWS - PRODUCES_STATE for REM, MAINTAINS_STATE for NREM. Cleanest demonstration in the project that causal role is a property of the STATE, not of the molecule.

cells.ambiguity: The measured construct is 'accumulation of sleep pressure', which builds during WAKE and is read out as SWA during NREM. MAINTAINS_STATE (regulates depth once entered) and CONTROLS_ENTRY (sets homeostatic drive to enter) are both defensible readings. Assigned MAINTAINS_STATE because the measurement is made within the state.

mechanisms.label: Astrocytic SNARE-dependent gliotransmission sets extracellular adenosine and sleep pressure

roles.basis: Genetic inhibition of gliotransmission attenuates accumulation of sleep pressure measured as NREM slow wave activity - i.e. it sets the depth of the state, not whether sleep occurs.

observed_effect.other: attenuated accumulation of sleep pressure measured as NREM SWA; cognitive deficits of sleep loss prevented

perturbations.statement: Inhibiting gliotransmission attenuated the accumulation of sleep pressure, assessed by measuring the slow wave activity of the EEG during NREM sleep, and prevented cognitive deficits associated with sleep loss.

observed_effect.other: sleep-suppressing effects of CPT were PREVENTED in dnSNARE mice; ICV CPT in wild type mimicked the transgenic phenotype - a double dissociation

perturbations.statement: The sleep-suppressing effects of the A1 receptor antagonist CPT were prevented following inhibition of gliotransmission and... intracerebroventricular delivery of CPT to wild-type mice mimicked the transgenic phenotype.

chain.step: SNARE-dependent vesicular release from astrocytes
regulation of extracellular adenosine
A1 receptor activation; sleep pressure and NREM SWA

mechanisms.proximal_physical_effect: vesicular release of a gliotransmitter, raising extracellular adenosine and thereby receptor-mediated inhibition

cells.discriminating_experiment: Separate the wake-accumulation and within-state components: measure SWA after matched prior wake duration in dnSNARE and control mice, to determine whether the role is MAINTAINS_STATE or CONTROLS_ENTRY.
cells.notes: THE GLIAL TEST CASE, AND v2 PASSES IT WITHOUT A GLIA CLASS. Per section 15A the question is what proximal physical effect the glial mechanism produces: here it is vesicular release, which is class 5. Cell type is recorded as metadata in the label and chain, not as a class. This is the same class that carries syntaxin in the worm anaesthesia row and dgk-1 in worm L1 sleep - and in all three the proximal effect really is release machinery. No forced assignment. Nadjar 2013 (PMID:23378051) independently implicates astrocyte-derived adenosine in sleep pressure during inflammatory challenge.

cells.ambiguity: The NOPR agonist result is pharmacological induction across three species including mouse; it demonstrates sufficiency of receptor activation to produce the state but does not establish that endogenous N/OFQ signalling normally produces it. PE-5 R2: Wake/NREM transition control is attributed to OX2R specifically, and the SAME paper shows the REM phenotype is not carried by OX2R alone - see the matching entry at S3_rem_mmus c6. PE-5 R2: THE STATE AND ITS CONTROLLER COME APART. CD73-KO mice sleep MORE at baseline yet show NO rebound after deprivation, and IL1beta still increases their NREM - so the machinery for entering NREM is intact and only the homeostatic drive is lost. The IL1beta arm is the positive control that makes the null interpretable, which is the standard this table's negative_assay_statement field demands. REM was unaffected in every condition, so this is also a state-specific negative for S3_rem_mmus.

mechanisms.label: Nociceptin/orphanin-FQ receptor activation promotes NREM sleep and slow wave activity

roles.basis: Two structurally distinct NOPR agonists dose-dependently produce NREM sleep in mice, rats and macaques - receptor activation is sufficient to generate the state.
The same manipulation dose-dependently increases EEG slow wave activity, i.e. the depth of the state, separately from its occurrence.

observed_effect.other: REM sleep SUPPRESSED; hypothermia and reduced locomotor activity at the highest dose; animals remained immediately arousable

perturbations.statement: We found a profound, dose-related increase in non-Rapid Eye Movement (NREM) sleep and electroencephalogram (EEG) slow wave activity (SWA) and suppression of Rapid Eye Movement sleep (REM) sleep in all three species. At the highest dose tested in rats, the increase in NREM sleep and EEG SWA was accompanied by a prolonged inhibition of REM sleep, hypothermia, and reduced locomotor activity.

chain.step: NOPR agonist binding
increased c-Fos in anterodorsal preoptic and parastrial GABAergic nuclei
increased NREM and SWA; REM suppressed

mechanisms.proximal_physical_effect: GPCR-mediated inhibition in preoptic and parastrial circuits; downstream hypothermia and reduced locomotion

mechanisms.label: OX2R activation is required for normal wake-to-NREM transition control

roles.basis: Germline receptor deletion produces behaviourally abnormal attacks of non-REM sleep; the authors attribute wake/non-REM transition control specifically to OX2R.

observed_effect.other: abnormal non-REM 'sleep attacks'; OX2R loss eliminates orexin-evoked excitation of histaminergic neurons that gate non-REM sleep onset

perturbations.statement: Both OX2R(-/-) and orexin(-/-) mice are similarly affected with behaviorally abnormal attacks of non-REM sleep ("sleep attacks") and show similar degrees of disrupted wakefulness. In contrast, OX2R(-/-) mice are only mildly affected with cataplexy-like attacks of REM sleep, whereas orexin(-/-) mice are severely affected... While normal regulation of wake/non-REM sleep transitions depends critically upon OX2R activation, the profound dysregulation of REM sleep control unique to the narcolepsy-cataplexy syndrome emerges from loss of signaling through both OX2R-dependent and OX2R-independent pathways.

chain.step: OX2R deletion
loss of orexin-evoked excitation of histaminergic neurons
uncontrolled non-REM sleep onset

mechanisms.proximal_physical_effect: loss of peptidergic excitatory drive onto histaminergic wake-promoting neurons

mechanisms.label: CD73-derived extracellular adenosine is required for the homeostatic NREM response to sleep deprivation, not for baseline NREM

roles.basis: Knockout abolishes the deprivation-induced NREM increase while baseline NREM is if anything GREATER - an effect on the entry controller that is separable from the state itself.

observed_effect.other: baseline NREMS GREATER in KO; NO NREMS enhancement after sleep deprivation; IL1beta STILL enhanced NREMS in KO (positive control for sleep-response capacity); 1.0-2.5 Hz power rise after deprivation smaller in KO; REM unchanged between strains in all conditions

perturbations.statement: Duration of spontaneous non-rapid eye movement sleep (NREMS) was greater in CD73-knockout (KO) mice than in C57BL/6 controls... After sleep deprivation (SD), NREMS was enhanced in controls but not CD73-KO mice. Interleukin-1 beta (IL1beta) enhanced NREMS in both strains, indicating that the CD73-KO mice were capable of sleep responses... Rapid eye movement sleep did not differ between strains in any of the experimental conditions.

chain.step: Nt5e/CD73 deletion
loss of extracellular AMP-to-adenosine conversion
absent homeostatic NREM rebound

mechanisms.proximal_physical_effect: loss of activity-dependent extracellular adenosine accumulation that raises sleep propensity

cells.discriminating_experiment: Test NOPR knockout or antagonist for a necessity phenotype. Current evidence is sufficiency only.
cells.notes: CROSS-STATE NOTE OF DIRECT RELEVANCE TO THE REM ROW: the same manipulation that PRODUCES deep NREM SUPPRESSES REM. One neuromodulatory mechanism, opposite signs for the two sleep states. This is the sharpest single piece of evidence in the stress test that 'sleep' is not one mechanistic category.

cells.ambiguity: POLARITY REVERSES WITH STIMULATION FREQUENCY. Photostimulation of the same neurons at 1-4 Hz promotes sleep; above 8 Hz it causes conduction block and WAKING. Earlier high-frequency studies had therefore reported the paradoxical opposite result. PE-5 R2: A NEGATIVE THAT IS MORE INFORMATIVE THAN MOST POSITIVES. A node of the sleep-promoting circuitry is REQUIRED for volatile-anaesthetic hypnosis (S5_ga_volatile_mmus c7) and DISPENSABLE for the amount and homeostasis of natural NREM sleep. It directly constrains the 'anaesthesia co-opts sleep circuitry' hypothesis: co-option is not symmetric, and a shared node can be load-bearing in one direction only. SCOPE: one node, not the circuit class; nothing here licenses a general claim about sleep circuitry being dispensable for NREM.
cells.negative_assay_statement: EEG-defined sleep and the homeostatic sleep drive after sleep deprivation were measured in PZGABA-ablated and mCherry control mice (PMID:40240218). Ablation of up to 70-80% of PZGABA neurones did not alter the amount of endogenous sleep or wakefulness and did not affect homeostatic sleep drive. The same animals, in the same study, showed a large and dose-graded behavioural anaesthetic phenotype, so the preparation had demonstrated power to resolve an effect of that manipulation. SCOPE: this null applies to the PZGABA node only; the cell remains POSITIVE overall on the strength of the VLPO galanin mechanism (PMID:30297727).

mechanisms.label: VLPO galanin neurons causally induce sleep and heat loss

roles.basis: Bidirectional causal test: optogenetic inhibition reduces sleep, chemogenetic and low-frequency optogenetic activation increase it, including short-latency sleep induction in an insomnia model.

observed_effect.other: sleep at 1-4 Hz; conduction block and WAKING above 8 Hz

perturbations.statement: Photostimulation of VLPOGAL neurons in mice promotes sleep with low frequency stimulation (1-4 Hz), but causes conduction block and waking at frequencies above 8 Hz.
Optogenetic inhibition reduces sleep.

observed_effect.other: also REDUCES BODY TEMPERATURE; induces short-latency sleep in an insomnia model

perturbations.statement: Chemogenetic activation of VLPOGAL neurons confirms the increase in sleep, and also reduces body temperature. In addition, chemogenetic activation of VLPOGAL neurons induces short-latency sleep in an animal model of insomnia.

chain.step: VLPO galanin neuron activity
sleep induction
heat loss / reduced body temperature

mechanisms.proximal_physical_effect: firing of a preoptic sleep-active population; downstream suppression of wake-promoting regions and increased heat loss

mechanisms.label: Parafacial-zone GABAergic neurons are NOT required for the amount of natural NREM sleep or for sleep homeostasis

roles.basis: TESTED AND NEGATIVE on sleep amount and on homeostatic rebound, with an internal positive control (a large anaesthetic phenotype) in the same animals.

observed_effect.other: no insomnia; sleep pressure after deprivation unchanged; 70-80% of PZGABA neurons destroyed; the SAME animals were behaviourally resistant to isoflurane and sevoflurane

perturbations.statement: Despite confirming that PZGABA ablation reduced the potency of two distinct volatile anaesthetics behaviourally, ablation did not alter the amount of endogenous sleep or wakefulness, nor did it affect the homeostatic sleep drive after sleep deprivation, and it did not produce EEG signatures of anaesthetic resistance during isoflurane exposure... destruction of up to 70-80% of PZGABA neurones was sufficient to alter anaesthetic susceptibility behaviourally without causing insomnia or altering sleep pressure.

chain.step: AAV-caspase ablation of parafacial GABAergic neurons
no change in NREM amount or homeostatic drive

mechanisms.proximal_physical_effect: no resolvable change in endogenous sleep amount or sleep pressure

overlap_resolution.justification: Not merely the same class - the same neurons, ablation, animals and paper. The rows differ only in which state was assayed. The cleanest available demonstration that causal role is a property of the STATE.

cells.discriminating_experiment: Dissociate the sleep and thermoregulatory outputs of VLPO-GAL neurons by projection-specific manipulation, to test whether hypothermia is required for sleep induction or a parallel output.
cells.notes: POLARITY IS CONTEXT_DEPENDENT AND THE CONTEXT IS THE STIMULATION PARAMETER, NOT THE BIOLOGY. This is a different kind of context-dependence from the worm cases (which were timing- and readout-dependent) and the frozen vocabulary handles it, but the distinction between a biological context and a methodological artefact of the tool is not representable. Flagged. Venner 2019 (PMID:31761703) documents an inhibitory lateral hypothalamic-preoptic circuit mediating rapid arousals, i.e. the opposing arm, not scored here.

cells.ambiguity: CLASS ASSIGNMENT IS ARGUABLE AND IS FLAGGED RATHER THAN RESOLVED. Funato 2016 establish SIK3 as a homeostatic regulator of sleep amount but do not establish its proximal physical effect. Placed in class 8 by parallel with the worm KIN-29/SIK cell (S2_core_cele c8), which had explicit energy-charge evidence. Class 9 is the live alternative, since SIK-family kinases act through HDAC/CRTC transcriptional regulators and the worm chain already records hda-4 as a class-9 upstream step. The frozen ontology has no class for a homeostatic signalling kinase.

mechanisms.label: SIK3 protein kinase sets inherent sleep need

roles.basis: Acts on the homeostatic regulation of sleep AMOUNT and inherent sleep need, not on whether sleep occurs; sleep deprivation changes phosphorylation of regulatory sites on the kinase.

observed_effect.other: splicing mutation; profound decrease in total wake time via increased inherent sleep need; identified in an unbiased mutagenesis screen

perturbations.statement: A splicing mutation in the Sik3 protein kinase gene causes a profound decrease in total wake time, owing to an increase in inherent sleep need. Sleep deprivation affects phosphorylation of regulatory sites on the kinase, suggesting a role for SIK3 in the homeostatic regulation of sleep amount. Sik3 orthologues also regulate sleep in fruitflies and roundworms.

chain.step: Sik3 splicing mutation
increased inherent sleep need; decreased total wake time

molecules.name: Sik3
molecules.ortholog_relation: Salt-inducible kinase family. C. elegans KIN-29 is scored in S2_core_cele c8 and is described by its own source as the C. elegans homolog of mammalian SIK. Funato 2016 state directly that Sik3 orthologues regulate sleep in roundworms. Orthology recorded, NOT used to score.

mechanisms.proximal_physical_effect: kinase-mediated phosphorylation signalling that sets homeostatic sleep pressure; downstream physical effector not established

cells.discriminating_experiment: Determine SIK3's proximal effector in mouse - transcriptional (HDAC/CRTC) versus metabolic - which would settle the class-8 vs class-9 assignment and make the worm/mouse comparison exact rather than orthology-level.
cells.notes: ADDED BY AMENDMENT (Entry 6). THE STRONGEST EXACT-MOLECULAR CROSS-SPECIES OVERLAP IN THE PROJECT, and unlike most such claims it does not rest on my own orthology inference: Funato 2016 state in the abstract that Sik3 orthologues regulate sleep in roundworms, and the worm cell's own source calls KIN-29 the C. elegans SIK homolog. Same molecular family, same broad role (homeostatic regulation of sleep amount), same polarity (PROMOTES_STATE), in worm lethargus and mouse NREM.

cells.ambiguity: ROLE ASSIGNMENT IS THE POINT HERE. The deletion is embryonic and the phenotype is adult, so the frozen role is BUILDS_MACHINERY alongside MAINTAINS_STATE - the animal's capacity for the state was built wrong, rather than its ongoing control being perturbed. Only two BUILDS_MACHINERY assignments existed in this table before, both in C. elegans; this is the first mammalian one, and it is carried by the ORTHOLOGUE of one of them (APTF-1).

mechanisms.label: AP-2 transcription factor Tfap2b acts embryonically in GABAergic neurons to build the machinery for normal sleep

roles.basis: The authors state Tfap2b acts during EARLY EMBRYONIC stages, and the adult phenotype follows a developmental alteration of GABAergic gene expression. Under the frozen role definitions this is construction of the machinery, not moment-to-moment control of the state.
Cell-type-restricted deletion shortens the time spent in the state and weakens its characteristic oscillation, at baseline and in rebound.

observed_effect.other: shortened NREM sleep time and reduced delta power; weaker delta and theta power during REBOUND sleep after 6 h deprivation; GABAergic genes (GAD1, GAD2, Vgat) downregulated in cortex, brainstem and cerebellum but UPREGULATED in striatum; heterozygous whole-animal deletion also reduces sleep

perturbations.statement: We previously found that AP2 transcription factors control sleep in C. elegans, Drosophila, and mice. Heterozygous deletion of Tfap2b, one of the mammalian AP2 paralogs, reduces sleep in mice... In mice, Tfap2b acts during early embryonic stages... During baseline conditions, Vgat-tfap2b-/- mice exhibited both shortened NREM and REM sleep time and reduced delta and theta power. Consistently, weaker delta and theta power were observed during rebound sleep in the Vgat-tfap2b-/- mice after sleep deprivation. Taken together, the results indicate that Tfap2b in GABAergic neurons is required for normal sleep.

chain.step: Tfap2b deletion in Vgat-expressing GABAergic neurons
altered embryonic brain patterning and GABAergic gene expression
reduced GABAergic inhibitory capacity in cortex, brainstem and cerebellum
shortened sleep time and weakened sleep oscillations

molecules.name: Tfap2b (AP-2beta)
molecules.ortholog_relation: DIRECT ORTHOLOGUE of C. elegans APTF-1, which already carries this table's S2_core_cele class-9 entry as the transcriptional specifier of the RIS sleep neuron. The authors state explicitly that AP2 transcription factors control sleep in C. elegans, Drosophila AND mice.

mechanisms.proximal_physical_effect: developmental specification of GABAergic sleep-promoting neurons, setting the inhibitory capacity available to the adult

overlap_resolution.justification: APTF-1 and Tfap2b are orthologous AP-2 transcription factors, both assigned BUILDS_MACHINERY, both acting developmentally on the GABAergic sleep-promoting population, in species separated by ~600 Myr. This is the single deepest mechanism correspondence in the table and the only one where the ROLE is conserved along with the molecule.

cells.notes: Sleep-homeostasis-associated transcriptional changes are well documented but were not located as a causal mechanism of SWS in a primary mouse study in this pass.

cells.ambiguity: Whether the thermal change is a mechanism OF sleep or a parallel output of the same neurons is not resolved by the evidence. Kroeger 2018 establish that one population causes both; they do not establish that heat loss causes sleep. PE-5 R2: REQUIRED BUT NOT SUFFICIENT, demonstrated in one paper by two manipulations pointing opposite ways: ablation removes the temperature-to-sleep coupling, while chemogenetic activation OR inhibition changes nothing about the sleep-wake cycle on its own. None of the six instantiated roles fits this cleanly - it is neither production, maintenance, entry control in the unconditional sense, protection, construction, nor exit. THIS IS THE STRONGEST CANDIDATE YET FOR INSTANTIATING THE RESERVED ROLE `PERMISSIVE_BACKGROUND`, and it is deliberately NOT instantiated here: one paper is not enough to open a frozen role, and doing so on a single result is precisely the kind of ontology drift the freeze discipline exists to stop. Recorded as a pending ontology decision with a named trigger: instantiate `PERMISSIVE_BACKGROUND` when a SECOND independent required-but-not-sufficient result appears in any row. Scored meanwhile as CONTROLS_ENTRY with context_dependence 'thermal_challenge_dependent', which is accurate but under-describes it. CLASS 11 SCOPE: this row's class-11 cell now carries BOTH directions of the thermal coupling - sleep-active preoptic neurons driving heat loss, and ambient temperature driving sleep through the DMH. The absence of a thermal phenotype axis (A_therm) is felt here again.

mechanisms.label: Sleep-active preoptic neurons causally drive heat loss; pharmacological NREM induction produces hypothermia

roles.basis: The same causal manipulation that induces sleep also lowers body temperature; the authors state the findings establish a causal role in BOTH sleep induction and heat loss.

perturbations.statement: Chemogenetic activation of VLPOGAL neurons confirms the increase in sleep, and also reduces body temperature... these findings establish a causal role of VLPOGAL neurons in both sleep induction and heat loss.
At the highest dose tested in rats, the increase in NREM sleep and EEG SWA was accompanied by a prolonged inhibition of REM sleep, hypothermia, and reduced locomotor activity.

chain.step: VLPO galanin neuron activation
increased heat loss, reduced body temperature

mechanisms.proximal_physical_effect: centrally driven increase in heat loss producing a decrease in core body temperature

mechanisms.label: Dorsomedial hypothalamic GABAergic neurons are required for ambient temperature to modulate NREM sleep, but are not sufficient to drive it

roles.basis: Caspase ablation attenuates the change in sleep-wake behaviour produced by cold and warm exposure. The requirement is for the THERMAL CONTROL of entry, and the sufficiency test in the same paper is negative.

observed_effect.other: in wild type, cold (24-12 degC) increased wake and decreased NREM while warm (32-44 degC) increased NREM and decreased wake, relative to 28 degC; DMH and DMH-GABA lesions ATTENUATED that temperature-driven change and aggravated core-temperature fluctuation after warm exposure; chemogenetic activation OR inhibition of DMH GABAergic neurons did NOT affect the sleep-wake cycle

perturbations.statement: We found that cold exposure (24/20/16/12 degC) increased wakefulness and decreased non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep, while warm exposure (32/36/40/44 degC) increased NREM sleep and decreased wakefulness compared to 28 degC conditions in wild-type mice. Then, using non-specific and specific apoptosis, we found that lesions of whole DMH neurons and DMH gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA)-ergic neurons induced by caspase-3 virus aggravated the fluctuation of core body temperature after warm exposure and attenuated the change in sleep-wake behaviors during cold and warm exposure. However, chemogenetic activation or inhibition of DMH GABAergic neurons did not affect the sleep-wake cycle.

chain.step: caspase ablation of DMH GABAergic neurons
loss of the thermoregulatory relay between preoptic input and sleep-wake output
ambient temperature no longer modulates NREM amount

molecules.name: dorsomedial hypothalamic (DMH) GABAergic neurons
molecules.ortholog_relation: The other mammalian class-11 entries in this table are preoptic sleep-active neurons driving heat loss (S4_deep_mmus) and anaesthetic effects on thermoregulatory thresholds (S5_ga_volatile_hsap). This adds the reverse direction: temperature acting ON sleep, through a named hypothalamic relay.

mechanisms.proximal_physical_effect: loss of a hypothalamic relay that converts ambient thermal load into a shift in sleep-wake balance

cells.discriminating_experiment: Clamp body temperature during VLPO-GAL activation. If sleep induction survives temperature clamping, heat loss is a parallel output; if not, thermal change is part of the mechanism.
cells.notes: CLASS 11'S FIRST SCOREABLE CONTENT ANYWHERE IN THE TABLE. In all five worm rows it was NOT_APPLICABLE (poikilotherm); in REM it was APPLICABLE but untested in mouse. Here it is causally established, and critically it is CENTRALLY REGULATED heat loss - not an externally imposed temperature and not a passive downstream consequence. That is the distinction section 15B asked to be preserved, and the class as frozen does preserve it.

cells.ambiguity: A NESTED NEGATIVE INSIDE A POSITIVE, and the two must not be collapsed. Panx1-/- mice sleep LESS (waking up, slow-wave sleep down, most pronounced in the dark period), so the channel promotes the state. But sleep rebound after 6 h deprivation was UNCHANGED, so the homeostatic response machinery is intact. Compare the CD73 result at class 6 in this same row, which is the exact mirror image: baseline sleep UP, rebound ABSENT. Two manipulations of the same adenosine pathway dissociate baseline amount from homeostatic drive in OPPOSITE directions. CLASS ASSIGNMENT CAVEAT: pannexin1 is a channel of the innexin superfamily and sits in class 12 on structural grounds, but the authors' proposed mechanism is ATP efflux and downstream ADENOSINE signalling, which is class 6. Recorded as class 12 proximal with class 6 in the chain; the alternative reading is defensible and is stated here rather than hidden.
cells.negative_assay_statement: Sleep rebound after a 6 h sleep deprivation was measured in Panx1-/- and Panx1+/+ mice in the same study that resolved a significant baseline difference in waking and slow-wave sleep percentages. Rebound remained unchanged between genotypes, so the assay had demonstrated power in these animals.

mechanisms.label: Pannexin1 hemichannels promote slow-wave sleep, plausibly via ATP-derived extracellular adenosine, without contributing to sleep homeostasis

roles.basis: Germline knockout shifts the baseline proportion of slow-wave sleep and waking across the light/dark cycle.

observed_effect.other: significant increase in waking and decrease in slow-wave sleep, most pronounced in the dark period; sleep rebound after 6 h deprivation UNCHANGED; increased movement activity; altered vertical and horizontal pole performance

perturbations.statement: We found a significant increase in waking and a correspondent decrease in slow wave sleep percentages in the Panx1-/- animals. These changes were especially pronounced during the dark period... These findings are consistent with the hypothesis that extracellular adenosine is relatively depleted in Panx1-/- animals due to the absence of the ATP-permeable hemichannels. At the same time, sleep rebound after a 6-h sleep deprivation remained unchanged in Panx1-/- mice as compared to the control animals.

chain.step: Panx1 deletion
loss of ATP-permeable hemichannel efflux
reduced extracellular adenosine
reduced slow-wave sleep, increased waking

molecules.name: Pannexin1 (Panx1)
molecules.ortholog_relation: The worm rows carry innexins (unc-9, inx-6) at class 12. Pannexins are the vertebrate innexin superfamily members, so this is ORTHOLOGOUS_MOLECULE at superfamily level - but the worm entries act as electrical synapses while this one is proposed to act as a metabolite conduit. SAME SUPERFAMILY, DIFFERENT PHYSICAL FUNCTION.

mechanisms.proximal_physical_effect: loss of a hemichannel conduit for extracellular ATP and hence of activity-dependent adenosine accumulation

overlap_resolution.justification: Pannexin and innexin are the same protein superfamily across the protostome-deuterostome split. The correspondence is structural; the proposed physical function differs (metabolite conduit here, electrical coupling there), which is exactly why the resolution hierarchy separates ORTHOLOGOUS_MOLECULE from SAME_PATHWAY_MODULE.

cells.notes: No electrical-coupling mechanism of SWS located in mouse in this pass.

new_evidence_added: Entire row is new; not scored under v1.

ontology_flags_v2: THE THREE AXES ARE INSUFFICIENT FOR HOMEOTHERMS. Body temperature is a major, causally manipulated state variable here and has no axis. It is not behaviour, not neural activity, and not metabolic rate. Forcing it into A_met would violate the project's own separation rule. v2 can represent thermal MECHANISM (class 11) but not thermal PHENOTYPE. This is the clearest v3 candidate to emerge from the mammalian rows, and it will get worse in torpor and hibernation.

A_neu.rate_amplitude conflates field-potential AMPLITUDE with firing RATE, and in SWS they diverge: slow-wave amplitude increases while firing alternates between up and down states. Scored 'increased' with the divergence noted, but the sub-measure needs splitting or renaming.

NO A_neu SUB-MEASURE IS 'DECREASED' IN EITHER MAMMALIAN SLEEP ROW. The frozen sub-measures do not capture the reduction the naive framing means, which is reduced RESPONSIVENESS and reduced high-frequency content. A responsiveness sub-measure or an explicit spectral-band decomposition may be needed.
The glial test case PASSED without a glia class: astrocytic gliotransmission scored as class 5 by proximal physical effect, with cell type as metadata. No glia class is warranted on this evidence.

Class 7 polarity CONTEXT_DEPENDENT is driven by a METHODOLOGICAL parameter (stimulation frequency causing conduction block), not by biology. v2 cannot distinguish biological context-dependence from tool artefact.
